verses.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον
verses.transliteration: Kai anastan hapan to plēthos autōn ēgagon auton epi ton Pilaton
verses.literal: Then the whole council . . . rose and led Jesus away to Pilate
verses.literalPt: E, LEVANTANDO-SE toda a multidão deles, o levaram a Pilatos.

verses.original: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ κωλύοντα φόρους Καίσαρι διδόναι καὶ λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν Χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι
verses.transliteration: ērxanto de katēgorein autou legontes Touton heuramen diastrephonta to ethnos hēmōn kai kōlyonta phorous Kaisari didonai kai legonta heauton Christon basilea einai
verses.literal: And they began to accuse Him saying We found this man subverting our nation forbidding payment of taxes . . . to Caesar and proclaiming Himself to be Christ a King
verses.literalPt: E começaram a acusá-lo, dizendo: Havemos achado este pervertendo a nossa nação, proibindo dar o tributo a César, e dizendo que ele mesmo é Cristo, o rei.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη Σὺ λέγεις
verses.transliteration: Ho de Pilatos ērōtēsen auton legōn Sy ei ho Basileus tōn Ioudaiōn Ho de apokritheis autō ephē Sy legeis
verses.literal: So Pilate asked Him Are You the King of the Jews You have said so - Jesus replied
verses.literalPt: E Pilatos perguntou-lhe, dizendo: Tu és o Rei dos Judeus? E ele, respondendo, disse-lhe: Tu o dizes.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ
verses.transliteration: Ho de Pilatos eipen pros tous archiereis kai tous ochlous Ouden heuriskō aition en tō anthrōpō toutō
verses.literal: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds I find no basis for a charge against this man
verses.literalPt: E disse Pilatos aos principais dos sacerdotes, e à multidão: Não acho culpa alguma neste homem.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε
verses.transliteration: Hoi de epischyon legontes hoti Anaseiei ton laon didaskōn kath’ holēs tēs Ioudaias kai arxamenos apo tēs Galilaias heōs hōde
verses.literal: But they kept insisting . . . He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching He began in Galilee and has come all the way here
verses.literalPt: Mas eles insistiam cada vez mais, dizendo: Alvoroça o povo ensinando por toda a Judéia, começando desde a Galiléia até aqui.

verses.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Pilatos de akousas epērōtēsen ei ho anthrōpos Galilaios estin
verses.literal: When Pilate heard this he asked if the man was a Galilean
verses.literalPt: Então Pilatos, ouvindo falar da Galiléia perguntou se aquele homem era galileu.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις
verses.transliteration: kai epignous hoti ek tēs exousias Hērōdou estin anepempsen auton pros Hērōdēn onta kai auton en Hierosolymois en tautais tais hēmerais
verses.literal: And learning that Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction he sent Him . . . to Herod who himself . . . was in Jerusalem at that time
verses.literalPt: E, sabendo que era da jurisdição de Herodes, remeteu-o a Herodes, que também naqueles dias estava em Jerusalém.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν ἦν γὰρ ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον
verses.transliteration: Ho de Hērōdēs idōn ton Iēsoun echarē lian ēn gar ex hikanōn chronōn thelōn idein auton dia to akouein peri autou kai ēlpizen ti sēmeion idein hyp’ autou ginomenon
verses.literal: When Herod saw Jesus he was greatly pleased He had wanted to see Him for a long time because he had heard about Him and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle
verses.literalPt: E Herodes, quando viu a Jesus, alegrou-se muito; porque havia muito que desejava vê-lo, por ter ouvido dele muitas coisas; e esperava que lhe veria fazer algum sinal.

verses.original: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: epērōta de auton en logois hikanois autos de ouden apekrinato autō
verses.literal: Herod questioned Jesus at great length but He gave no answer . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: E interrogava-o com muitas palavras, mas ele nada lhe respondia.

verses.original: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Heistēkeisan de hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis eutonōs katēgorountes autou
verses.literal: Meanwhile the chief priests and scribes stood there vehemently accusing Him
verses.literalPt: E estavam os principais dos sacerdotes, e os escribas, acusando-o com grande veemência.

verses.original: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ
verses.transliteration: exouthenēsas de auton kai ho Hērōdēs syn tois strateumasin autou kai empaixas peribalōn esthēta lampran anepempsen auton tō Pilatō
verses.literal: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed . . . and mocked Him Dressing Him in a fine robe they sent Him back . . . to Pilate
verses.literalPt: E Herodes, com os seus soldados, desprezou-o e, escarnecendo dele, vestiu-o de uma roupa resplandecente e tornou a enviá-lo a Pilatos.

verses.original: Ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετ’ ἀλλήλων προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς αὑτούς
verses.transliteration: Egenonto de philoi ho te Hērōdēs kai ho Pilatos en autē tē hēmera met’ allēlōn proupērchon gar en echthra ontes pros hautous
verses.literal: That day - Herod and Pilate became friends - before this time they had been enemies . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: E no mesmo dia, Pilatos e Herodes entre si se fizeram amigos; pois dantes andavam em inimizade um com o outro.

verses.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ συνκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τὸν λαὸν
verses.transliteration: Pilatos de synkalesamenos tous archiereis kai tous archontas kai ton laon
verses.literal: Then Pilate called together the chief priests the rulers and the people
verses.literalPt: E, convocando Pilatos os principais dos sacerdotes, e os magistrados, e o povo,

verses.original: εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Προσηνέγκατέ μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὡς ἀποστρέφοντα τὸν λαόν καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ἀνακρίνας οὐθὲν εὗρον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ αἴτιον ὧν κατηγορεῖτε κατ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: eipen pros autous Prosēnenkate moi ton anthrōpon touton hōs apostrephonta ton laon kai idou egō enōpion hymōn anakrinas outhen heuron en tō anthrōpō toutō aition hōn katēgoreite kat’ autou
verses.literal: and said to them You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion I have examined Him here in your presence . . . and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhes: Haveis-me apresentado este homem como pervertedor do povo; e eis que, examinando-o na vossa presença, nenhuma culpa, das de que o acusais, acho neste homem.

verses.original: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ Ἡρῴδης ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου ἐστὶν πεπραγμένον αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: all’ oude Hērōdēs anepempsen gar auton pros hēmas kai idou ouden axion thanatou estin pepragmenon autō
verses.literal: Neither has Herod for he sent Him back . . . to us As you can see He has done nothing deserving of death
verses.literalPt: Nem mesmo Herodes, porque a ele vos remeti, e eis que não tem feito coisa alguma digna de morte.

verses.original: παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω
verses.transliteration: paideusas oun auton apolysō
verses.literal: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him
verses.literalPt: Castigá-lo-ei, pois, e soltá-lo-ei.
E era-lhe necessário soltar-lhes um pela festa.

verses.original: Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες Αἶρε τοῦτον ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν
verses.transliteration: Anekragon de pamplēthei legontes Aire touton apolyson de hēmin ton Barabban
verses.literal: But they all cried out in unison . . . Away with this man Release Barabbas to us
verses.literalPt: Mas toda a multidão clamou a uma, dizendo: Fora daqui com este, e solta-nos Barrabás.

verses.original: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ
verses.transliteration: hostis ēn dia stasin tina genomenēn en tē polei kai phonon blētheis en tē phylakē
verses.literal: (Barabbas . . . had been imprisoned . . . . . . . . . for an insurrection in the city and for murder
verses.literalPt: O qual fora lançado na prisão por causa de uma sedição feita na cidade, e de um homicídio.

verses.original: Πάλιν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος προσεφώνησεν αὐτοῖς θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: Palin de ho Pilatos prosephōnēsen autois thelōn apolysai ton Iēsoun
verses.literal: Wanting to release Jesus Pilate addressed them again
verses.literalPt: Falou, pois, outra vez Pilatos, querendo soltar a Jesus.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες Σταύρου σταύρου αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: hoi de epephōnoun legontes Staurou staurou auton
verses.literal: but they kept shouting . . . Crucify Him Crucify Him
verses.literalPt: Mas eles clamavam em contrário, dizendo: Crucifica-o, crucifica-o.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω
verses.transliteration: Ho de triton eipen pros autous Ti gar kakon epoiēsen houtos ouden aition thanatou heuron en autō paideusas oun auton apolysō
verses.literal: A third time he said to them What evil has this man done I have found in Him no offense worthy of death So after I punish Him I will release Him
verses.literalPt: Então ele, pela terceira vez, lhes disse: Mas que mal fez este? Não acho nele culpa alguma de morte. Castigá-lo-ei pois, e soltá-lo-ei.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de epekeinto phōnais megalais aitoumenoi auton staurōthēnai kai katischyon hai phōnai autōn
verses.literal: But they were insistent demanding with loud voices . . . for Jesus to be crucified And their clamor prevailed
verses.literalPt: Mas eles instavam com grandes gritos, pedindo que fosse crucificado. E os seus gritos, e os dos principais dos sacerdotes, redobravam.

verses.original: καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: kai Pilatos epekrinen genesthai to aitēma autōn
verses.literal: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met
verses.literalPt: Então Pilatos julgou que devia fazer o que eles pediam.

verses.original: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: apelysen de ton dia stasin kai phonon beblēmenon eis phylakēn hon ētounto ton de Iēsoun paredōken tō thelēmati autōn
verses.literal: As they had requested he released the one imprisoned . . . . . . for insurrection and murder and he handed Jesus over to their will
verses.literalPt: E soltou-lhes o que fora lançado na prisão por uma sedição e homicídio, que era o que pediam; mas entregou Jesus à vontade deles.

verses.original: Καὶ ὡς ἀπήγαγον αὐτόν ἐπιλαβόμενοι Σίμωνά τινα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ ἐπέθηκαν αὐτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν φέρειν ὄπισθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai hōs apēgagon auton epilabomenoi Simōna tina Kyrēnaion erchomenon ap’ agrou epethēkan autō ton stauron pherein opisthen tou Iēsou
verses.literal: As the soldiers led Him away . . . they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country and they put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus
verses.literalPt: E quando o iam levando, tomaram um certo Simão, cireneu, que vinha do campo, e puseram-lhe a cruz às costas, para que a levasse após Jesus.

verses.original: Ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ πολὺ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ γυναικῶν αἳ ἐκόπτοντο καὶ ἐθρήνουν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Ēkolouthei de autō poly plēthos tou laou kai gynaikōn hai ekoptonto kai ethrēnoun auton
verses.literal: A great number of people followed Him including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him
verses.literalPt: E seguia-o grande multidão de povo e de mulheres, as quais batiam nos peitos, e o lamentavam.

verses.original: στραφεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ μὴ κλαίετε ἐπ’ ἐμέ πλὴν ἐφ’ ἑαυτὰς κλαίετε καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: strapheis de pros autas ho Iēsous eipen Thygateres Ierousalēm mē klaiete ep’ eme plēn eph’ heautas klaiete kai epi ta tekna hymōn
verses.literal: But Jesus turned to them and said Daughters of Jerusalem do not weep for Me but weep for yourselves and for your children
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, voltando-se para elas, disse: Filhas de Jerusalém, não choreis por mim; chorai antes por vós mesmas, e por vossos filhos.

verses.original: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ἔρχονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς ἐροῦσιν Μακάριαι αἱ στεῖραι καὶ αἱ κοιλίαι αἳ οὐκ ἐγέννησαν καὶ μαστοὶ οἳ οὐκ ἔθρεψαν
verses.transliteration: hoti idou erchontai hēmerai en hais erousin Makariai hai steirai kai hai koiliai hai ouk egennēsan kai mastoi hoi ouk ethrepsan
verses.literal: Look the days are coming when people will say Blessed are the barren women the wombs that never bore and breasts that never nursed
verses.literalPt: Porque eis que hão de vir dias em que dirão: Bem-aventuradas as estéreis, e os ventres que não geraram, e os peitos que não amamentaram!

verses.original: τότε Ἄρξονται λέγειν τοῖς ὄρεσιν Πέσετε ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς Καὶ τοῖς βουνοῖς Καλύψατε ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: tote Arxontai legein tois oresin Pesete eph’ hēmas Kai tois bounois Kalypsate hēmas
verses.literal: At that time they will say to the mountains Fall on us and to the hills Cover us
verses.literalPt: Então começarão a dizer aos montes: Caí sobre nós, e aos outeiros: Cobri-nos.

verses.original: Ὅτι εἰ ἐν τῷ ὑγρῷ ξύλῳ ταῦτα ποιοῦσιν ἐν τῷ ξηρῷ τί γένηται
verses.transliteration: Hoti ei en tō hygrō xylō tauta poiousin en tō xērō ti genētai
verses.literal: For if men do these things while the tree is green what will happen when it is dry
verses.literalPt: Porque, se ao madeiro verde fazem isto, que se fará ao seco?

verses.original: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι κακοῦργοι δύο σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι
verses.transliteration: Ēgonto de kai heteroi kakourgoi dyo syn autō anairethēnai
verses.literal: Two others who were criminals were also led away to be executed with Jesus
verses.literalPt: E também conduziram outros dois, que eram malfeitores, para com ele serem mortos.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai hote ēlthon epi ton topon ton kaloumenon Kranion ekei estaurōsan auton kai tous kakourgous hon men ek dexiōn hon de ex aristerōn
verses.literal: When they came to the place called The Skull they crucified Him there along with the criminals one on His right and the other on His left
verses.literalPt: E, quando chegaram ao lugar chamado a Caveira, ali o crucificaram, e aos malfeitores, um à direita e outro à esquerda.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν Πάτερ ἄφες αὐτοῖς οὐ γὰρ οἴδασιν τί ποιοῦσιν διαμεριζόμενοι δὲ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἔβαλον κλήρους
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous elegen Pater aphes autois ou gar oidasin ti poiousin diamerizomenoi de ta himatia autou ebalon klērous
verses.literal: Then Jesus said Father forgive them for they do not know what they are doing And they divided up His garments by casting lots
verses.literalPt: E dizia Jesus: Pai, perdoa-lhes, porque não sabem o que fazem. E, repartindo as suas vestes, lançaram sortes.

verses.original: Καὶ εἱστήκει ὁ λαὸς θεωρῶν ἐξεμυκτήριζον δὲ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες λέγοντες Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν σωσάτω ἑαυτόν εἰ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἐκλεκτός
verses.transliteration: Kai heistēkei ho laos theōrōn exemyktērizon de kai hoi archontes legontes Allous esōsen sōsatō heauton ei houtos estin ho Christos tou Theou ho eklektos
verses.literal: The people stood watching and the rulers sneered at Him saying He saved others let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God the Chosen One
verses.literalPt: E o povo estava olhando. E também os príncipes zombavam dele, dizendo: Aos outros salvou, salve-se a si mesmo, se este é o Cristo, o escolhido de Deus.

verses.original: Ἐνέπαιξαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται προσερχόμενοι ὄξος προσφέροντες αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Enepaixan de autō kai hoi stratiōtai proserchomenoi oxos prospherontes autō
verses.literal: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine
verses.literalPt: E também os soldados o escarneciam, chegando-se a ele, e apresentando-lhe vinagre.

verses.original: καὶ λέγοντες Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων σῶσον σεαυτόν
verses.transliteration: kai legontes Ei sy ei ho Basileus tōn Ioudaiōn sōson seauton
verses.literal: If You are the King of the Jews they said save Yourself
verses.literalPt: E dizendo: Se tu és o Rei dos Judeus, salva-te a ti mesmo.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ καὶ ἐπιγραφὴ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ Ο ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΙΟΥΔΑΙΩΝ ΟΥΤΟΣ
verses.transliteration: Ēn de kai epigraphē ep’ autō HO BASILEUS TŌN IOUDAIŌN HOUTOS
verses.literal: Above Him was posted an inscription THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS
verses.literalPt: E também por cima dele, estava um título, escrito em letras gregas, romanas, e hebraicas: ESTE É O REI DOS JUDEUS.

verses.original: Εἷς δὲ τῶν κρεμασθέντων κακούργων ἐβλασφήμει αὐτόν λέγων Οὐχὶ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός σῶσον σεαυτὸν καὶ ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: Heis de tōn kremasthentōn kakourgōn eblasphēmei auton legōn Ouchi sy ei ho Christos sōson seauton kai hēmas
verses.literal: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him Are You not the Christ he said Save Yourself and us
verses.literalPt: E um dos malfeitores que estavam pendurados blasfemava dele, dizendo: Se tu és o Cristo, salva-te a ti mesmo, e a nós.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἕτερος ἐπιτιμῶν αὐτῷ ἔφη Οὐδὲ φοβῇ σὺ τὸν Θεόν ὅτι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ κρίματι εἶ
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de ho heteros epitimōn autō ephē Oude phobē sy ton Theon hoti en tō autō krimati ei
verses.literal: But the other one rebuked him saying Do you not even fear God since you are under the same judgment
verses.literalPt: Respondendo, porém, o outro, repreendia-o, dizendo: Tu nem ainda temes a Deus, estando na mesma condenação?

verses.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν δικαίως ἄξια γὰρ ὧν ἐπράξαμεν ἀπολαμβάνομεν οὗτος δὲ οὐδὲν ἄτοπον ἔπραξεν
verses.transliteration: kai hēmeis men dikaiōs axia gar hōn epraxamen apolambanomen houtos de ouden atopon epraxen
verses.literal: We are punished justly for we are receiving what our actions deserve But this man has done nothing wrong
verses.literalPt: E nós, na verdade, com justiça, porque recebemos o que os nossos feitos mereciam; mas este nenhum mal fez.

verses.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν Ἰησοῦ μνήσθητί μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν σου
verses.transliteration: kai elegen Iēsou mnēsthēti mou hotan elthēs eis tēn basileian sou
verses.literal: Then he said Jesus remember me when You come into Your kingdom
verses.literalPt: E disse a Jesus: Senhor, lembra-te de mim, quando entrares no teu reino.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀμήν σοι λέγω σήμερον μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ Παραδείσῳ
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autō Amēn soi legō sēmeron met’ emou esē en tō Paradeisō
verses.literal: And Jesus said to him Truly I tell you today you will be with Me in Paradise
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhe Jesus: Em verdade te digo que hoje estarás comigo no Paraíso.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης
verses.transliteration: Kai ēn ēdē hōsei hōra hektē kai skotos egeneto eph’ holēn tēn gēn heōs hōras enatēs
verses.literal: It was now about the sixth hour and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour
verses.literalPt: E era já quase a hora sexta, e houve trevas em toda a terra até à hora nona, escurecendo-se o sol;

verses.original: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον
verses.transliteration: tou hēliou eklipontos eschisthē de to katapetasma tou naou meson
verses.literal: The sun was darkened and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle
verses.literalPt: E rasgou-se ao meio o véu do templo.

verses.original: Καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Πάτερ εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν
verses.transliteration: Kai phōnēsas phōnē megalē ho Iēsous eipen Pater eis cheiras sou paratithemai to pneuma mou touto de eipōn exepneusen
verses.literal: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice . . . Father into Your hands I commit My Spirit And when He had said this He breathed His last
verses.literalPt: E, clamando Jesus com grande voz, disse: Pai, nas tuas mãos entrego o meu espírito. E, havendo dito isto, expirou.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ἐδόξαζεν τὸν Θεὸν λέγων Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν
verses.transliteration: Idōn de ho hekatontarchēs to genomenon edoxazen ton Theon legōn Ontōs ho anthrōpos houtos dikaios ēn
verses.literal: When the centurion saw what had happened he gave glory to God saying Surely this was a righteous man
verses.literalPt: E o centurião, vendo o que tinha acontecido, deu glória a Deus, dizendo: Na verdade, este homem era justo.

verses.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον
verses.transliteration: kai pantes hoi symparagenomenoi ochloi epi tēn theōrian tautēn theōrēsantes ta genomena typtontes ta stēthē hypestrephon
verses.literal: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened they returned home beating their breasts
verses.literalPt: E toda a multidão que se ajuntara a este espetáculo, vendo o que havia acontecido, voltava batendo nos peitos.

verses.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα
verses.transliteration: heistēkeisan de pantes hoi gnōstoi autō apo makrothen kai gynaikes hai synakolouthousai autō apo tēs Galilaias horōsai tauta
verses.literal: But all . . . those who knew Jesus including the women who had followed Him from Galilee stood at a distance watching these things
verses.literalPt: E todos os seus conhecidos, e as mulheres que juntamente o haviam seguido desde a Galiléia, estavam de longe vendo estas coisas.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων καὶ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος
verses.transliteration: Kai idou anēr onomati Iōsēph bouleutēs hyparchōn kai anēr agathos kai dikaios
verses.literal: Now there was a Council member named Joseph a good and righteous man
verses.literalPt: E eis que um homem por nome José, senador, homem de bem e justo,

verses.original: οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συνκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: houtos ouk ēn synkatatetheimenos tē boulē kai tē praxei autōn apo Harimathaias poleōs tōn Ioudaiōn hos prosedecheto tēn basileian tou Theou
verses.literal: who had not consented to their decision or action He was from the Judean town . . . . . . of Arimathea and was waiting for the kingdom of God
verses.literalPt: Que não tinha consentido no conselho e nos atos dos outros, de Arimatéia, cidade dos judeus, e que também esperava o reino de Deus;

verses.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: houtos proselthōn tō Pilatō ētēsato to sōma tou Iēsou
verses.literal: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus
verses.literalPt: Esse, chegando a Pilatos, pediu o corpo de Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος
verses.transliteration: kai kathelōn enetylixen auto sindoni kai ethēken auton en mnēmati laxeutō hou ouk ēn oudeis oupō keimenos
verses.literal: Then he took it down wrapped it in a linen cloth and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock where no one . . . had yet been laid
verses.literalPt: E, havendo-o tirado, envolveu-o num lençol, e pô-lo num sepulcro escavado numa penha, onde ninguém ainda havia sido posto.

verses.original: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν Παρασκευῆς καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν
verses.transliteration: kai hēmera ēn Paraskeuēs kai sabbaton epephōsken
verses.literal: It was Preparation Day and the Sabbath was beginning
verses.literalPt: E era o dia da preparação, e amanhecia o sábado.

verses.original: Κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Katakolouthēsasai de hai gynaikes haitines ēsan synelēlythuiai ek tēs Galilaias autō etheasanto to mnēmeion kai hōs etethē to sōma autou
verses.literal: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed
verses.literalPt: E as mulheres, que tinham vindo com ele da Galiléia, seguiram também e viram o sepulcro, e como foi posto o seu corpo.

verses.original: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν
verses.transliteration: hypostrepsasai de hētoimasan arōmata kai myra Kai to men sabbaton hēsychasan kata tēn entolēn
verses.literal: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes And they rested on the Sabbath according to the commandment
verses.literalPt: E, voltando elas, prepararam especiarias e ungüentos; e no sábado repousaram, conforme o mandamento.
